author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Indonesian rescuers are searching the Sunda Strait for eight people whose speedboat lost contact while traveling to Anak Krakatau to cover volcanic activity.

The group includes five photojournalists, two crew members and a route guide, the Associated Press reported. The boat departed Carita in Banten province, and relatives received its last known message at 6:13 p.m. Monday saying the group had reached waters near the island.

Their last reported position was about 18.5 kilometers, or roughly 11.5 miles, from shore. Search teams deployed Tuesday had not established contact or confirmed the boat’s location by early Wednesday. The journalists work for several Indonesian and international news organizations, with one described as a freelance photographer.

Anak Krakatau’s initial eruption ended Sunday, but the volcano has continued intermittent activity involving explosions, lava and ash. Officials had not established whether that activity, weather, mechanical failure or another cause was connected to the disappearance. The search remains active, and early details may change as rescue crews cover the area and review communications.
dek: A speedboat carrying five photojournalists, two crew members and a guide lost contact while traveling to report on the Indonesian volcano.
headline: Search underway for eight missing near Anak Krakatau
